quote_cursor_repair_contract.legacy_v2_policy_reason: An omitted expired quote can contain the greatest allocated sequence, so retained quotes and journals do not uniquely reconstruct the next sequence.

cursor_records.expired_entry_policy: Ordinary expired quote payloads may be omitted. An expired quote bound to a pending-discard session remains persisted. Either policy preserves the consumed identity space through next_quote_sequence.
cursor_records.restore_policy: Card-inventory v3 must restore the exact persisted integer before another quote allocation. The value must be greater than every retained or journaled market-quote sequence. Card-inventory v2 is rejected with allocator_cursor_missing_requires_backup; it is never defaulted to 1 or inferred from retained quotes.
cursor_records.next_allocation_test: Create a lower retained quote, allocate and omit a higher expired quote, restore, then assert that the next quote ID and fingerprint equal an uninterrupted fork and that no expired quote ID is reused.

cursor_records.expired_entry_policy: Not applicable. Listing identity continuation is retained by refill_sequence, while current racks and transaction lineage retain materialized listings and slot revisions.
cursor_records.restore_policy: Restore refill_sequence and slot_revisions_by_region exactly through RegionSupplyRuntimeController strict preflight and apply. No other owner may allocate a normal-card listing ID or supply revision.
cursor_records.next_allocation_test: After restore, refill the same legal slot in forked runs and assert identical item_id, refill_sequence, slot revision, rack revision, and owner fingerprint.

cursor_records.expired_entry_policy: Not applicable. Exact-once completion and inflight lineage are validated against the saved sequence.
cursor_records.restore_policy: Strictly restore the nonnegative transaction_sequence together with completed, inflight, and pending-settlement lineage; reject a sequence that precedes any retained execution ID.
cursor_records.next_allocation_test: Restore a nontrivial execution section, allocate the next execution in both restored and uninterrupted forks, and assert identical execution ID with no duplicate transaction.

cursor_records.expired_entry_policy: Not applicable. The next sequence and terminal state-port journal are persisted even though transient reservations must be absent at a legal checkpoint.
cursor_records.restore_policy: Strictly restore the positive next_reservation_sequence through the card-inventory commodity child and production state-port contract. Repeated apply must not advance it.
cursor_records.next_allocation_test: Restore the same state-port payload in forked runs, reserve the same transaction, and assert identical reservation ID; repeated apply and rollback retain the exact cursor.

derived_identity_records.expired_entry_policy: No transaction cursor is discarded or reconstructed. The transaction identity is determined by the quote ID; preserving the quote cursor preserves the future transaction namespace.
derived_identity_records.restore_policy: Do not add or default an independent transaction cursor. Recompute only from the authoritative restored quote ID and validate any materialized journal identity against it.
derived_identity_records.next_allocation_test: Use the first post-restore quote for a real purchase and assert that district-purchase:<quote_id> equals the uninterrupted fork transaction ID.

derived_identity_records.expired_entry_policy: Not applicable. A materialized card instance is saved by the session owner; a future instance derives from authoritative listing and transaction identities.
derived_identity_records.restore_policy: Do not create an independent card-instance cursor. Existing instances restore from session state, and new purchase instances derive from the restored listing item ID and deterministic purchase transaction ID.
derived_identity_records.next_allocation_test: Complete the same post-restore purchase in forked runs and assert identical runtime_instance_id, transaction journal fingerprint, and session owner fingerprint.
